name: commerce_set3_p1
label: Commerce: set 3 (money, finance, law and modern commerce)

papers.title: Money and Currency: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on money and currency, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The main problem of barter that money solves as a medium of exchange is
questions.explanation:
Under barter each trader must want exactly what the other has; money ends that search.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the need for banks: Banks developed after money, not as a problem of barter.
- the high cost of advertising: Advertising is unrelated to barter.
- the use of cheques: Cheques are a form of bank money, not a barter problem.

questions.stem: When the price of a bag of rice is stated in leones, money is acting as
questions.explanation:
Money provides a common unit in which the value of every good is stated as a price.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a store of value: A store of value means holding money to spend later.
- a standard of deferred payment: That is about stating future payments in money.
- a medium of exchange: That is money being used to pay for goods.

questions.stem: The quality of money that makes it difficult to forge is
questions.explanation:
Good money is easily recognised and hard to copy.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- divisibility: Divisibility means it can be split into smaller units.
- portability: Portability means it is easy to carry.
- durability: Durability means it lasts a long time.

questions.stem: Money that must by law be accepted in settlement of debts is
questions.explanation:
Notes and coins issued by the Bank of Sierra Leone are legal tender.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- near money: Near money, such as treasury bills, is not a means of payment.
- commodity money: Commodity money is goods such as cowries or salt.
- bank money: Bank money is moved by cheque or transfer and may be refused.

questions.stem: After the 2022 redenomination, what is the price in new leones of a bag of rice that cost Le 450,000?
questions.explanation:
1,000 old leones = 1 new leone, so 450,000 ÷ 1,000 = NLe 450.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 450000 NLe: That is the old price; three zeros were removed.
- 4500 NLe: You divided by 100 instead of 1,000.
- 45 NLe: You divided by 10,000 instead of 1,000.

questions.stem: The price index rises from 100 in the base year to 125. What is the value of NLe 1 in base-year terms?
questions.explanation:
Value of money $= \dfrac{100}{125} \times 1 = $ NLe 0.80: a 20% fall in purchasing power.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 1.25 NLe: You divided the index by 100; the value of money is 100 ÷ index.
- 0.75 NLe: You subtracted the 25% rise from 1; that overstates the fall.
- 0.25 NLe: That is the rise in prices as a fraction, not the value of money.

questions.stem: During inflation, the group most likely to gain is
questions.explanation:
Debtors repay loans with money that buys less than when they borrowed it.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- creditors: Creditors are repaid in money worth less.
- pensioners on fixed incomes: Fixed incomes buy less as prices rise.
- savers: Savings lose purchasing power.

questions.stem: An importer must pay 4,000 US dollars. The exchange rate is 1 US dollar = NLe 24. How much is this in leones?
questions.explanation:
Cost in leones $= 4000 \times 24 = $ NLe 96,000.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 166.67 NLe: You divided by the exchange rate instead of multiplying.
- 4024 NLe: You added the exchange rate.
- 100000 NLe: You used a rate of NLe 25 to the dollar.

papers.title: Insurance: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on insurance, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The principle that requires both parties to disclose all material facts is
questions.explanation:
Uberrimae fidei: hiding a material fact makes the contract voidable.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- indemnity: Indemnity restores the insured to their former position.
- subrogation: Subrogation passes the insured's rights to the insurer after a claim.
- contribution: Contribution makes several insurers share a loss.

questions.stem: A person can insure a shop only if they would suffer financial loss from its destruction. This is the principle of
questions.explanation:
You may insure your own shop, but not your neighbour's.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- proximate cause: Proximate cause concerns the main cause of a loss.
- utmost good faith: That concerns disclosure of facts.
- contribution: That concerns sharing a loss among insurers.

questions.stem: After paying a claim for a car damaged in an accident, the insurer sues the driver who caused it. This is
questions.explanation:
The insurer takes over the insured's rights against third parties.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- indemnity: Indemnity is the compensation itself.
- reinsurance: Reinsurance is passing part of a risk to another insurer.
- double insurance: That is insuring the same property with two insurers.

questions.stem: Which of these risks is NOT insurable?
questions.explanation:
Losses from fashion changes cannot be calculated from past records, so they are borne by the entrepreneur.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Fire in a warehouse: Fire is insurable.
- Theft of stock by burglars: Burglary is insurable.
- Damage to goods at sea: Marine losses are insurable.

options.label: A
options.content: Loss from a change in fashion

questions.stem: The type of motor insurance required by law is
questions.explanation:
Third-party cover protects other people injured or whose property is damaged by the vehicle.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- comprehensive insurance: Comprehensive cover is optional, though wider.
- fidelity guarantee: Fidelity guarantee covers dishonest employees.
- life assurance: Life assurance is not motor insurance.

questions.stem: Insurance against loss caused by dishonest employees is
questions.explanation:
Fidelity guarantee covers theft or fraud by cashiers, storekeepers and other staff.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- burglary insurance: Burglary insurance covers theft by forced entry.
- public liability insurance: That covers injury to the public on the premises.
- consequential loss insurance: That covers lost profit after a fire.

questions.stem: Goods worth NLe 80,000 are insured for NLe 60,000. A fire causes a loss of NLe 20,000. How much does the insurer pay under the average clause?
questions.explanation:
Claim $= \dfrac{60000}{80000} \times 20000 = $ NLe 15,000.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 20000 NLe: You paid the full loss; the goods were under-insured.
- 60000 NLe: That is the sum insured, not the claim.
- 26666.67 NLe: You turned the fraction upside down (value ÷ sum insured).

questions.stem: A warehouse worth NLe 400,000 is insured against fire at NLe 5 per NLe 1,000. What is the annual premium?
questions.explanation:
Premium $= \dfrac{400000}{1000} \times 5 = $ NLe 2,000.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 2000000 NLe: You multiplied the value by 5 without dividing by 1,000.
- 80000 NLe: You divided by 5 instead of multiplying the number of thousands by 5.
- 400 NLe: That is the number of thousands, not the premium.

papers.topic: The Stock Exchange and Capital Market
papers.title: The Stock Exchange and Capital Market: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on the stock exchange and capital market, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The stock exchange is mainly a market for
questions.explanation:
It is a secondary market where investors buy and sell shares, debentures and bonds already issued.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- new bank notes: Notes are issued by the central bank.
- short-term treasury bills only: Treasury bills belong to the money market.
- foreign currency: Foreign currency is traded in the foreign exchange market.

questions.stem: A speculator who buys shares expecting their prices to rise is a
questions.explanation:
Bulls buy now to sell later at a higher price.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- bear: A bear sells, expecting prices to fall.
- stag: A stag buys new issues to sell quickly.
- lame duck: A lame duck cannot meet commitments.

questions.stem: A person who applies for newly issued shares hoping to sell them at a profit as soon as dealing begins is a
questions.explanation:
Stags speculate on new issues in the primary market.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- bull: A bull buys existing shares expecting a general rise.
- bear: A bear sells expecting prices to fall.
- jobber: A jobber is a dealer who trades on their own account.

questions.stem: Debenture holders are
questions.explanation:
A debenture is a long-term loan to a company at a fixed rate of interest.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- owners of the company: Shareholders are the owners.
- directors of the company: Directors manage the company.
- paid only when there is profit: Debenture interest must be paid even in a loss.

options.label: D
options.content: paid only when there is profit

questions.stem: Which shareholders usually have voting rights?
questions.explanation:
Ordinary shareholders control the company: one vote per share.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Preference shareholders: They usually have no voting rights.
- Debenture holders: Debenture holders are creditors, not shareholders.
- Treasury bill holders: Treasury bills are government securities.

questions.stem: A company has NLe 30,000 to pay as ordinary dividend on 200,000 shares of NLe 1 each. What is the dividend per share?
questions.explanation:
Dividend per share $= 30000 \div 200000 = $ NLe 0.15 (a 15% dividend on a NLe 1 share).

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 6.67 NLe: You divided the shares by the dividend.
- 0.30 NLe: You divided by 100,000 shares instead of 200,000.
- 1.50 NLe: You divided by 20,000 shares instead of 200,000.

questions.stem: A share with a par value of NLe 1 pays a dividend of NLe 0.12 and sells for NLe 2 on the exchange. What is the dividend yield?
questions.explanation:
Dividend yield $= \dfrac{0.12}{2} \times 100 = 6\%$.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 12 %: That is the dividend as a percentage of par value, not of market price.
- 1666.67 %: You divided the price by the dividend.
- 24 %: You multiplied the dividend by the price.

questions.stem: An investor buys 2,000 shares at NLe 1.50 each. Brokerage is 1.5% of the cost and other charges are NLe 25. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation:
Cost $= 2000 \times 1.50 = 3000$; brokerage $= 1.5\% \times 3000 = 45$; total $= 3000 + 45 + 25 = $ NLe 3,070.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 3000 NLe: You left out the brokerage and other charges.
- 3045 NLe: You left out the other charges of NLe 25.
- 3475 NLe: You charged 15% brokerage instead of 1.5%.

papers.title: Legal Aspects of Business: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on legal aspects of business, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Goods displayed in a shop window with price tags are, in law,
questions.explanation:
A display invites customers to make offers, which the seller may accept or refuse.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- an offer: The customer makes the offer at the till.
- an acceptance: Acceptance comes from the seller.
- a binding contract: No contract exists until the seller accepts the customer's offer.

questions.stem: Something of value given by each party to a contract is called
questions.explanation:
Consideration: the price, goods, services or promises exchanged.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- capacity: Capacity is the legal ability to contract.
- consent: Consent is genuine agreement.
- legality: Legality means the purpose must be lawful.

questions.stem: A contract induced by misrepresentation is
questions.explanation:
It is valid until the injured party chooses to cancel (rescind) it.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- void from the start: A void contract has no legal effect at all.
- illegal: An illegal contract has an unlawful purpose.
- always valid and enforceable: The injured party may cancel it.

questions.stem: A court order to carry out the terms of a contract is
questions.explanation:
Used where money is not an adequate remedy, such as the sale of a particular plot of land.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- an injunction: An injunction stops a party from doing something.
- damages: Damages are money compensation.
- quantum meruit: This is payment for work already done.

questions.stem: A contract ends because the goods to be sold were destroyed by flood before delivery. This discharge is by
questions.explanation:
An event beyond the parties' control made performance impossible.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- performance: Performance is when both sides do what they promised.
- breach: Breach is a party failing to perform; nobody is at fault here.
- agreement: Agreement is when both sides choose to end it.

questions.stem: When a principal later approves a contract made by an agent without authority, agency is created by
questions.explanation:
Ratification gives the agent's act the same effect as if it had been authorised.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- necessity: Agency of necessity arises in an emergency.
- estoppel: Estoppel arises when the principal leads others to believe someone is their agent.
- express appointment: Express appointment is made before the agent acts.

questions.stem: Under hire purchase, ownership of the goods passes to the buyer
questions.explanation:
Until then the buyer is a hirer and the seller may repossess on default.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- when the deposit is paid: The buyer gets possession, not ownership, on paying the deposit.
- when the agreement is signed: That is a credit sale.
- never: Ownership passes at the final payment.

options.label: C
options.content: when the last instalment is paid

questions.stem: A freezer costs NLe 6,000 cash, or a 20% deposit and 12 monthly instalments of NLe 480 on hire purchase. What is the hire purchase charge?
questions.explanation:
Deposit $= 1200$; HP price $= 1200 + 12 \times 480 = 6960$; charge $= 6960 - 6000 = $ NLe 960.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 6960 NLe: That is the hire purchase price, not the extra charge.
- 5760 NLe: That is the total of the instalments.
- 1200 NLe: That is the deposit, not the hire purchase charge.

papers.title: Consumer Protection: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on consumer protection, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Mixing sand with grain before selling it is an example of
questions.explanation:
Adulteration lowers quality by adding cheaper substances.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- hoarding: Hoarding is holding goods back to raise prices.
- price discrimination: That is charging different prices to different groups.
- branding: Branding gives a product a name and identity.

questions.stem: The consumer's right to a refund, repair, replacement or compensation for faulty goods is the right to
questions.explanation:
Redress means a fair settlement of genuine complaints.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- choose: The right to choose is about access to a variety of goods.
- be informed: The right to be informed is about accurate information.
- a healthy environment: That concerns pollution.

questions.stem: In Sierra Leone, the body that registers medicines and seizes fake drugs is
questions.explanation:
The Pharmacy Board licenses pharmacies, registers drugs and removes fake or expired medicines.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the Sierra Leone Standards Bureau: The Standards Bureau sets and tests product standards.
- the National Revenue Authority: The NRA collects taxes.
- SALPOST: SALPOST provides postal services.

options.label: B
options.content: the Pharmacy Board of Sierra Leone

questions.stem: Which is a responsibility of the consumer?
questions.explanation:
Receipts are needed to seek redress; checking dates avoids expired goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Fixing the prices of goods in markets: Consumers do not fix prices.
- Issuing standards for products: That is the Standards Bureau's role.
- Licensing pharmacies: That is the Pharmacy Board's role.

options.label: A
options.content: Fixing the prices of goods in markets

options.label: C
options.content: Keeping receipts and checking expiry dates

questions.stem: Consumers need protection mainly because
questions.explanation:
One buyer knows less and has less power than a large seller or a monopoly.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- sellers always charge the lowest prices: Some sellers exploit consumers.
- all goods are tested before sale: Many goods are not tested.
- advertising is always accurate: Some advertising misleads.

options.label: A
options.content: sellers always charge the lowest prices

options.label: B
options.content: all goods are tested before sale

options.label: D
options.content: they often lack information and bargaining power compared with sellers

questions.stem: Producers protect consumers through self-regulation when they
questions.explanation:
Codes of conduct, quality control, guarantees and after-sales service protect buyers and reputations.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- hoard goods to raise prices: That exploits consumers.
- remove expiry dates from packs: That harms consumers.
- refuse to accept complaints: That denies redress.

options.label: A
options.content: adopt codes of conduct and give guarantees

questions.stem: A measure sold as 2 kg of rice for NLe 40 actually holds 1.6 kg. What is the true price per kilogram?
questions.explanation:
True price $= 40 \div 1.6 = $ NLe 25 per kg, not NLe 20: a hidden 25% price rise.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 20 NLe: That is the price per kilogram the consumer believes they pay.
- 64 NLe: You multiplied the price by the true weight.
- 5 NLe: That is the overcharge per kilogram, not the true price.

questions.stem: A function of a consumer association is to
questions.explanation:
They also test products, expose bad practice and press government for better laws.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- manufacture goods for members: Consumer associations do not produce goods.
- collect import duties: That is customs.
- issue the national currency: That is the central bank.

options.label: B
options.content: educate consumers and take up their complaints

papers.title: Government Policies and Business: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on government policies and business, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The transfer of a government-owned enterprise to private owners is
questions.explanation:
In Sierra Leone it is managed by the National Commission for Privatisation, set up in 2002.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- nationalisation: Nationalisation is the opposite: private to government.
- commercialisation: Commercialisation keeps the enterprise in government ownership.
- indigenisation: Indigenisation transfers ownership from foreigners to citizens.

questions.stem: A government enterprise told to cover its costs and make a profit without subsidy, while remaining state-owned, has been
questions.explanation:
Commercialisation changes how the enterprise is run, not who owns it.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- privatised: Privatisation transfers ownership to private owners.
- nationalised: Nationalisation brings a private firm into state ownership.
- indigenised: Indigenisation concerns foreign and citizen ownership.

questions.stem: A policy to transfer the ownership and control of businesses from foreigners to citizens is
questions.explanation:
Nigeria's Indigenisation Decrees of the 1970s are the best-known West African example.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- privatisation: Privatisation moves state firms to private owners of any nationality.
- deregulation: Deregulation removes rules that limit competition.
- nationalisation: Nationalisation moves ownership to the state.

questions.stem: A main reason for nationalisation is to
questions.explanation:
Strategic and essential services are brought under public control.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- reduce government control of the economy: Nationalisation increases government control.
- raise money by selling state assets: That is a reason for privatisation.
- encourage foreign ownership: Nationalisation reduces foreign ownership.

options.label: A
options.content: reduce government control of the economy

options.label: B
options.content: control strategic industries such as power and water

options.label: C
options.content: raise money by selling state assets

questions.stem: A radio costs NLe 400 before Goods and Services Tax at 15%. What does the consumer pay?
questions.explanation:
GST $= 15\% \times 400 = 60$. Price $= 400 + 60 = $ NLe 460.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 60 NLe: That is the tax alone.
- 340 NLe: You subtracted the tax instead of adding it.
- 415 NLe: You added NLe 15 instead of 15%.

questions.stem: Which government agency in Sierra Leone promotes investment and helps exporters find markets?
questions.explanation:
The Sierra Leone Investment and Export Promotion Agency supports investors and exporters.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NASSIT: NASSIT runs social security.
- NATCOM: NATCOM regulates telecommunications.
- SALPOST: SALPOST provides postal services.

questions.stem: A rise in interest rates by the central bank is most likely to
questions.explanation:
Monetary policy works through the cost of credit.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- make loans cheaper: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive.
- increase government tax revenue directly: Interest rates are monetary policy, not tax.
- remove all import duties: Interest rates do not affect duties.

options.label: D
options.content: make loans dearer and reduce business investment

questions.stem: A feature of a public corporation is that it is
questions.explanation:
Examples include Guma Valley Water Company and the Sierra Leone Ports and Harbours Authority.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- owned by shareholders who buy its shares on the stock exchange: That describes a public limited company.
- run by a sole proprietor: A sole proprietor owns a small private business.
- free from any accountability to Parliament: It is accountable through the minister.

options.label: A
options.content: owned by the state and set up by an Act of Parliament

options.label: B
options.content: owned by shareholders who buy its shares on the stock exchange

options.label: D
options.content: free from any accountability to Parliament

papers.topic: E-Commerce and Modern Trends in Commerce
papers.title: E-Commerce and Modern Trends in Commerce: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on e-commerce and modern trends in commerce, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A wholesaler taking online orders from retailers is an example of
questions.explanation:
Both the wholesaler and the retailers are businesses.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce: B2C sells to individual final buyers.
- consumer-to-consumer (C2C) e-commerce: C2C is individuals selling to each other.
- government-to-citizen (G2C) e-commerce: G2C is government services online.

questions.stem: Selling used phones to other individuals through a Facebook group is
questions.explanation:
Individuals trade with each other through an online platform.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- business-to-business (B2B) e-commerce: No business is involved on either side.
- business-to-government (B2G) e-commerce: No government is involved.
- franchising: Franchising is using another firm's brand for a fee.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of e-commerce to consumers is that
questions.explanation:
Buyers rely on photos and descriptions, and risk fraud or poor quality.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- they can shop at any time: That is an advantage.
- prices are easy to compare: That is an advantage.
- goods are delivered to the door: That is an advantage.

options.label: A
options.content: they can shop at any time

options.label: C
options.content: goods are delivered to the door

options.label: D
options.content: goods cannot be inspected before buying

questions.stem: An arrangement in which a firm lets another business use its name and methods for a fee and royalties is
questions.explanation:
The franchisor supplies the brand and system; the franchisee pays fees and royalties.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- outsourcing: Outsourcing is hiring outside firms for tasks.
- containerisation: Containerisation is moving goods in standard boxes.
- agency banking: Agency banking lets shops act for banks.

questions.stem: A machine in a shop that lets customers pay with a card is a
questions.explanation:
POS terminals let shops accept card payments, so they hold less cash.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- automated teller machine (ATM): ATMs are mainly for cash withdrawals.
- franking machine: Franking machines print postage.
- vending machine: Vending machines sell goods directly.

questions.stem: Someone claiming to be from a mobile network asks for your one-time code (OTP). You should
questions.explanation:
Real networks and banks never ask for your PIN or OTP.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- send the code so they can fix your account: Anyone with the OTP can take your money.
- send half of the code: No part of the code should be shared.
- reply with your PIN instead: The PIN must never be shared either.

options.label: A
options.content: send the code so they can fix your account

questions.stem: A trader sells 120 dresses a month online at NLe 150 each; each costs NLe 100. She pays NLe 10 delivery per order and NLe 400 for data and adverts. What is her monthly net profit?
questions.explanation:
$120 \times (150 - 100 - 10) - 400 = 4800 - 400 = $ NLe 4,400.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 6000 NLe: That is the gross profit before delivery and data costs.
- 5600 NLe: You left out the delivery charges.
- 4800 NLe: You left out the data and advertising cost.

questions.stem: Which is a problem of e-commerce in Sierra Leone?
questions.explanation:
Without formal addresses, deliveries depend on landmarks and phone calls.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Too many delivery riders in every village: Delivery services are limited outside towns.
- Mobile money is not used anywhere: Mobile money is widely used.
- Network coverage is perfect everywhere: Coverage is poor in many rural areas.

options.label: A
options.content: Too many delivery riders in every village

options.label: B
options.content: Mobile money is not used anywhere

options.label: D
options.content: Lack of street addresses for delivery
